newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ low rate policy still positive for economy-MOF.
newsitem.headline: BOJ low rate policy still positive for economy-MOF.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) current low interest rate policy still has positive effects on the economy, Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We believe the effects of the low rate (policy) are spreading to various sectors (of the economy). It still has positive effects," Komura said in an interview.
He added that policy on the official discount rate (ODR) was solely in the hands of the BOJ and refrained from commenting on the outlook for the ODR.
The vice minister also said recent rises in Japan's current account surplus were a temporary phenomenon brought about by the effects of a sales tax increase in April.
"It's a short-term phenomenon," Komura said, adding that the surplus was unlikely to continue rising.
Asked if he believed that the surplus would decrease or that the tempo of its climb would slow heading into the autumn, Komura said: "I think it (the surplus) will follow that path."
Komura also reiterated Japan's policy of seeking domestic demand-led growth.
"There is no change in our stance of seeking to strengthen a recovery led by domestic demand," he said.
He added that in order to achieve this goal, the ministry will push ahead with deregulation and structural reform of the economy.
On the domestic economy, Komura said Japan's recovery was continuing, backed by firm private-sector demand.
He also said the effects of the sales tax rise were within expectations.

"The effects of the tax rise were largely within expectations... Private consumption is recovering gradually as well as capital spending. So although the tempo (of the recovery) may slow temporarily, the economy is continuing to recover on the back of firm private-sector demand," Komura said.
